newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle priced $65, no bids -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle priced $65, no bids -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners priced cattle at $65.00 per cwt, but no bids were reported so far, several feedlot sources said.

"We've got a few buyers out looking around and I imagine they'll bid $62.00," a Panhandle-area feedlot manager said. "But, right now, everyone is waiting to see if hog futures will lift the cattle," he said.
CME pork complex futures were seen sharply higher to limit-up following a government quarterly inventory survey, which showed farmers planned on holding back fewer-than-expected hogs for breeding.

If cattle futures are able to gather spillover strength from the pork complex, fed cattle prices this week were seen trading at least steady with last week at $63.00 to possibly $1.00 higher, cattle feeders said.
Owners were losing $20.00 per head or more, at $63.00 and would be close to even at $64.00, sources said.
Sales were expected early this week, likely on Tuesday, as packers and owners try to get their business completed before the Independence Day holiday on Friday, they said.
Wheat harvesting was in full swing in southwestern Kansas following rain delays last week, sources said.
Wheat prices reportedly were near a level that could make it attractive to include in feed rations, they said.
"People are talking about it, but I'm not sure they're using the wheat yet," a Kansas feedlot manager said.
